findings.title: Radar visual void
findings.where: Arena and Road, bottom-left UI panels
findings.problem: The radar is a completely featureless black circle with only a center pointer, lacking any grid lines, sweep animation, or peripheral data.
findings.why: It conveys no sense of scale or proximity to threats, rendering it an inert decorative element rather than a functional tactical instrument.
findings.fix: Add subtle radial grid lines and a sweeping indicator line that pulses; plot blips for the player's current heading and potential nearby enemies.

findings.title: Map surface illegibility
findings.problem: The ground texture is a repetitive, low-contrast grayscale tile pattern that lacks visual depth or clear navigation markers.
findings.why: It creates a 'floating' effect where the car and buildings don't feel grounded in the world, making the city layout feel abstract rather than spatial.
findings.fix: Introduce subtle environmental details like cracked asphalt textures, road paint, or localized debris patches to break up the repetitive tiling and define pathways.

findings.title: Data-heavy panel strain
findings.where: Arena and Road, right-hand condition monitors
findings.problem: The 'Condition' and 'Tyres' panels use high-density text and thin, low-contrast progress bars that blend into the panel background.
findings.why: During combat or high-speed transit, a player cannot glance at their status to assess damage; they have to stop and squint, breaking the flow.
findings.fix: Increase the contrast of the status bars (using a brighter, distinct color like yellow or white) and increase the font weight for critical values like armor counts.

findings.title: UI container lack of hierarchy
findings.problem: The list of vehicle components is presented as a uniform white-on-dark text block with no visual separation between categories (e.g., core parts vs. weapons).
findings.why: It forces the player to parse the entire list to find specific parts, making the constructor feel like a spreadsheet rather than a workshop.
findings.fix: Add subtle background fill colors or header dividers for component sections to group related parts and define a clear top-to-bottom reading order.

findings.title: Low-contrast main CTA
findings.problem: The 'New Driver' and 'Controls' buttons use a dark-teal-on-dark-gray color scheme that lacks the luminance necessary to pop against the background.
findings.why: It is not immediately obvious that these are the primary interaction points for the user, delaying the 'start' process.
findings.fix: Apply a subtle outer glow or a brighter border stroke to the active button and increase the contrast ratio of the white text against the menu's background color.
